wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: no resource-authorisation object is involved; the property is over the tokens a caller's options become on the git command line
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: there is one direction (caller option to git argv); the guarded operations are not a role or peer pair
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: every operation here is a write sink (process spawn or file write) and the tests assert its side effect, so a read-only guard cannot pass
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the candidate builder runs before the git process starts and there is no normalising step between the caller's value and argv
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the decision is made from the option tokens alone; there is no authority or secret lookup that can return nothing

traps.shape: an option-shaped value carried by a single-character keyword argument when short options are rendered separately, as a scalar or a sequence
traps.realistic_because: the reported route; the shared candidate builder screens only the keyword name, so the value token that git will parse as an option is never seen

traps.shape: the same shared candidate builder backs another public operation whose option writes a caller-chosen filesystem path
traps.realistic_because: one file away from the reported call and reached through the same builder; the reported operation names clone, and an output option writes a file rather than running a command, so it reads as out of scope

traps.shape: a remote-listing option alias that runs a caller-chosen program is absent from the per-subcommand blocklist
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the blocklist names only the better-known upload-pack spelling, so a solver who sees that entry treats the operation as covered

traps.shape: an operation that takes caller keywords and passes them to git has no option screening at all, while sibling revision operations do
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the comparison looks read-only and its keywords look like developer flags, but the forwarded options include one that writes a caller-chosen path

traps.shape: the legitimate joined rendering of a one-character option next to the attacker's joined value: attached safe values and a numeric similarity threshold must stay accepted while a joined option character is refused

traps.realistic_because: the split/joined knob and the numeric similarity value are public, tested behaviour, so an over-broad rule that scans every character of a short token or forbids the joined mode breaks real use
